capabilities.target: vendor master record, including bank details

inputs.source: Supplier invoice uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The agent updates vendor bank details whenever 'the invoice shows new bank details', treating untrusted invoice content as sufficient grounds for a sensitive master-data change, with no independent verification step specified in the instructions.

The only safeguard named in the prompt is a model-written one-line approval summary. Nothing requires that summary to disclose that a bank change occurred or to flag a mismatch, so the safeguard's substance depends entirely on the model's own judgment of what to include.

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The approver sees only the model's one-line summary, not the raw action (runtime notes: bank account numbers and change history are not shown). Per control_decay.md, a model_summary approval gate is partially_dependent and fails under model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, and control_removal; a more persuasive model writes more convincing summaries, and ~150 approvals/day invites approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403).

controls.name: Out-of-band callback verification of new bank details using vendor contact info from the trusted vendor master, not the invoice
Raw action review showing full account number diff and vendor master change history, instead of a model summary
Cooldown or secondary approval for any payment scheduled within N days of a bank detail change on the same vendor
Scope the ERP credential to the vendors and amounts in the current invoice batch rather than any vendor and any payment

findings.title: TC9: Summary-gated approval lets an invoice-asserted bank change reach an irreversible payment

attack_path.note: Untrusted invoice uploaded to the supplier portal asserts new bank details
Agent updates vendor master bank details per invoice content, gated only by a one-line model summary
Agent schedules payment, possibly to the just-changed account, gated by the same kind of summary approval

findings.residual_rationale: Rubric step 2 credit for a model_summary approval gate would floor residual at moderate, but the approval card discloses neither the bank account number nor the change history (runtime notes), so the clerk cannot detect that a bank change occurred, let alone verify it, even in principle. This is weaker than an ordinary model-summary gate and combines with ~150 approvals/day inviting fatigue, so residual is rated high rather than the moderate floor.

forecast.watch_signal: Model or platform version bump with no separate review (subject.model.swappable=true), any change to the approval card template, or rising approval volume/pressure that further erodes clerk scrutiny.

evidence.observation: Agent updates vendor bank details based on invoice content and only requests a one-line summary approval before payment or bank change.
The example card shows only payee, amount, and invoice/PO match. It gives no indication that a bank detail change occurred, no account number, and no change history.
Bank account numbers and change history are not shown to the clerk; the clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day; the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review.

recommendations.action: Require out-of-band verification (a phone call to a vendor contact already on file, not a number from the invoice) before applying any bank detail change.
Replace the model-summary approval card with a raw-action review showing the full bank account change (old vs new) and a link to the vendor master change history.
Block or require secondary approval for any payment scheduled within N days of a bank detail change on the same vendor.

findings.title: TC4: Broad ERP credential lets an untrusted invoice alter payment routing for any vendor

attack_path.note: Agent matches/reads vendor master using a credential scoped to any vendor
The same broad credential can update bank details for any vendor, not only the one on the current invoice

findings.residual_rationale: This capability is itself the bank-change approval point. The rubric step 2 credit for a model_summary gate would floor residual at moderate, but the same card design omits the account number and change history for this exact action, so the gate cannot meaningfully evaluate the change it is supposed to approve. Residual is therefore rated high, matching the uncredited inherent risk for this path.

forecast.watch_signal: Approval gate removed or narrowed, credential scope widened without re-review, or new vendor data sources added without tightening credential_scope.

evidence.observation: The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment, not only ones related to the current invoice batch, which is broader than the task's least-privilege need.
The agent is instructed to update vendor records directly from invoice-asserted bank details, invoking the broad credential on untrusted input.

recommendations.action: Scope the ERP credential to least privilege: limit update/payment actions to vendors and amounts present in the invoice batch under processing, with a separate elevated credential for out-of-band fixes.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: an untrusted supplier invoice can trigger a vendor bank-detail change and an irreversible payment (S3 sink) through an ERP credential scoped to any vendor and any payment. Residual is high rather than the moderate floor a model-summary approval gate would normally earn, because the approval card in this design omits exactly the fact a reviewer would need to catch fraud: it shows neither the bank account number nor the change history, for either the bank-change or payment approval. Forecast rises to critical if the model is upgraded, autonomy is increased, or the approval gate is removed or narrowed, since that gate is the only control standing between the untrusted invoice and the payment sink.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, the approval card example, and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP/tool manifest, IaC, or ERP permission export was provided; capability scope (credential_scope, data_sensitivity) is inferred from the runtime notes and prompt text, so exact credential boundaries carry residual uncertainty despite the explicit statement that the credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment.
No logging or audit control was described in the artifacts. If one exists but was not documented, detective coverage may be understated; if none exists, repudiation risk is understated.
